slides.title: Digital Image Representation

visualInspection.notes: Grayscale/binary use common 2D representation and RGB common (H,W,3). Pixel dtype distinctions uint8, float32 and bool viewed with images and pixel-grid inset. Float32 is not inherently normalized; casting alone does not scale. uint8 0 black255white applies grayscale, not each color-plane value as complete white. RGB is a stated common layout, not every possible color image convention. Inset 10x10 values descriptive, not full standalone source-image data. Actual full 1800-pixel page and footer viewed.

slides.title: Point Operations

slides.title: Point Operations - Histogram Equalization

visualInspection.notes: Histogram equalization uses cumulative distribution mapping; actual plotted green distribution is spiky and sparse, not flat. Discrete equal-intensity pixels all map together so exactly uniform output is not guaranteed. Contrast may improve for narrow distributions but noise can amplify and no guarantee every image benefits. Screenshot O=I.normhist(). Fixed mapping applied pointwise, estimation uses global image histogram. Actual full 1800-pixel page and footer viewed.

slides.title: Application of point operations

visualInspection.notes: Color-to-mono maps3vector toscalar, not simply red-plane extraction in general; threshold valley heuristic between modes not universal optimum; linear normalization can stretch existing distinctions but cannot restore clipped information. Gamma encode/decode uses nonlinear intensity mapping; sRGB is piecewise and should not be reduced silently to one universal pure-power formula. No coefficients or exact sRGB transfer function taught on this slide. Actual full 1800-pixel page and footer viewed.

slides.title: Operators – Convolution

visualInspection.notes: Convolution uses image offsets(u-i,v-j), equivalent to correlation with kernel rotated180degrees, not transposealone. Actual grayscale kernel diagram confirms both-axis reversal. Equality for centrosymmetrickernels K(i,j)=K(-i,-j), not merelymatrix-symmetric K=K^T. Convolution theorem requires compatible boundary/padding convention; unpadded discrete FFT multiplication yields circular behavior, so no unspecified universal output-shape claim. Sourcepreferredsuperiormathematicalproperties is qualitative, not universalruntimebenchmark. Actual full 1800-pixel page and footer viewed.
